text:
mira: Quick heads-up — we're observing slow steady KV cache memory growth on Dedicated over long context runs, but the same workload on Hosted stabilizes. Private/on-prem shows more fragmentation and higher page fault rates. Dropping the profiler summary and configs below.

jason: Can you paste the reproducer + kernel/driver versions?

mira: repro is the longcontext stress harness: `./tools/kv_stress --seq-len=8192 --clients=12 --duration=8h`. Dedicated runs on 2xA100 VPC (driver 535.XX, kernel 6.1), Hosted uses 4xA10s (driver 535.XX, kernel 5.15), Private is older 3090-based onprem (driver 470.103, kernel 5.10).

eli: interesting — different kernels + drivers could change page cache behavior. Any jemalloc/hw config differences?

mira: yes — notable diffs we found after a few runs:
```
# Dedicated (reserved)
kv.eviction.threshold = 0.55
kv.page_align = false
malloc_conf = "oversize_threshold:1,lg_dirty_mult:4"

# Hosted
kv.eviction.threshold = 0.7
kv.page_align = true
malloc_conf = "oversize_threshold:2,lg_dirty_mult:2"

# Private/onprem
kv.eviction.threshold = 0.6
kv.page_align = false
malloc_conf = "oversize_threshold:1,lg_dirty_mult:8"
```

mira: Also capturing perf counters (first 6h window):
```
Dedicated: minor-faults=12.2k, major-faults=410, pgpgin=3.2M, pgpgout=1.8M
Hosted:   minor-faults=7.3k,  major-faults=180, pgpgin=1.1M, pgpgout=0.9M
Private:  minor-faults=18.4k, major-faults=980, pgpgin=4.8M, pgpgout=3.9M
```

sarah: Those pgpgin/out deltas are huge for Private — suggests frequent page reclaim/paging. Could be MTU/NUMA/driver differences causing higher fragmentation and more frequent evict cycles.

jason: Also check kernel transparent hugepages and MADV_FREE behavior — some kernels will collapse pages differently which affects our KV slab lifespan.

mira: I listed the main hypothesis in-thread:
- Kernel/driver differences -> page fragmentation + madvise semantics differ.
- jemalloc config + lg_dirty_mult -> different dirty page reclamation cadence.
- kv.eviction.threshold lower on Dedicated (0.55) triggers more aggressive evictions but we still see growth — maybe reallocation churn + slab fragmentation.
- Hosted has higher threshold + page_align true -> better reuse of frames for long contexts.

eli: Can we instrument the runtime to emit: per-tenant slab fragmentation ratio, eviction churn rate (evicts/sec), and avg slot reuse time? We had similar telemetry for earlier batching work.

mira: I added a runtime flag `--kv-instrument=frag,evict,slotreuse` and pushed a build to the integration cluster. Early traces: Dedicated shows frag_ratio ~0.42 -> grows to 0.61 after 4h. Hosted stays ~0.28 -> 0.30. Private starts 0.38 -> 0.7 with high variance.

ops-oncall: infra-bot reports: `deploy: integrate/kv-instrument -> integration` succeeded at 2321109000 :white_check_mark:

jason: Nice. Next steps: capture a side-by-side heap/profile and a `pagemap` snapshot at the 0h/4h/8h marks. Also run Dedicated with `kv.page_align = true` and `malloc_conf` matched to Hosted to see if behaviour follows config or hardware.

mira: On it. Quick experiment results so far (2h runs):
- Dedicated + page_align=true: frag growth reduced (0.61 -> 0.45 at 2h), minor-faults down ~30%
- Dedicated + malloc_conf matched to Hosted: additional 12% improvement
- Private still noisy; suspect driver+NUMA tuning + PCIe peer config is causing pinned frame churn

sarah: Can we try toggling `kv.eviction.threshold` upward on Dedicated to 0.68 as a controlled canary? If higher threshold reduces churn and keeps reuse higher, that's telling. But watch latency tail — higher threshold might increase memory usage and occasional GC spikes.

mira: I ran threshold=0.68 for 6h. Observed: memory peak +8% vs baseline, but average evicts/sec fell 45%, tail latency unaffected for 99th p50->p99 diff ~+1ms. Frag ratio stabilized ~0.33.

eli: suggests eviction cadence tuning could be more important than raw kernel differences in some cases. But Private still shows driver/kernel dominated behavior. We should codify two mitigations:
- Config profile: `hosted-compat` (page_align=true, malloc_conf=hosted, eviction_threshold=0.68) for Dedicated as opt-in.
- Runtime detection: if kernel/driver mismatch observed, enable `aggressive-coalesce` to reduce fragmentation at allocation time.

mira: Agree. Filing PERF ticket and PR to add `hosted-compat` profile + instrumentation. Will also open an infra ticket for Private onprem team to validate driver + NUMA/PIN settings.

ops-oncall: Created infra ticket INFRA-8781 for onprem driver/NUMA checks.

jason: Two asks for follow-up: include a short-run reproducer with `--trace-pagemap` output, and capture `perf mem` samples around hot allocs to see if specific code paths allocate noisy slab objects.

mira: Will attach the traces and link the PR. Preliminary perf samples point at `kv::alloc_map_chunk` and `kv::evict_candidate_scan` — looks like increased churn in candidate scanning when threshold is low.

sarah: Great work. If the hosted-compat profile looks stable, let's prepare a customer-facing blurb explaining Dedicated tuning options (tradeoff: slightly higher peak mem for lower steady evict churn and predictable tail latency).

mira: Noted. I'll update the docs draft after we merge the PR. Perf ticket PERF-1429 created and assigned to me + jason.

infra-bot: link: https://redwood.internal/p/perf/1429 :information_source:

mira: thanks all — I'll post the traces and PR link here once available. :thumbsup:
